mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate earnings, lowering the present value of future cash flows and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and remains >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified policy tightening, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 1% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the monthly payrolls figure signals weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market softening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or indistinguishable from baseline (p > 0.05) when the labor signal is present, or the signal is not observed.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it anticipates higher inflation expectations, prompting investors to demand higher risk premiums and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during such inflation surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months indicates strengthening supply capacity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified supply expansion, or the expansion lasts fewer than three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 2%, it signals a shift toward accommodative policy, which lowers real discount rates and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified policy shift.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% for two consecutive months indicates labor market weakness, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases above 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during the unemployment spike.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both retail sales proxy (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) suggest robust overall demand, which usually precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies show simultaneous increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly retail sales (HOUST) for three consecutive months indicates softening demand, which often precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during the sales decline.
